questions.q: In a Jupyter notebook, what determines which variables exist?
options: The order in which the cells appear on the page
The file name of the notebook
The order in which the cells are executed
Only the last cell in the notebook
questions.explain: Python remembers everything that has been run, in the order it was run — which can differ from the page order.
questions.evidence: it is the order of execution of cells that is important in a Jupyter notebook, not the order in which they appear.

questions.q: What does Python 3 do when an integer meets a float in arithmetic?
options: It automatically converts the integer to a float as needed
It rounds the float to an integer
questions.explain: That is why 1 / 2.0 gives 0.5.
questions.evidence: Python 3 automatically converts integers to floats as needed.

questions.q: What is a library in Python?
options: A list of every function name in Python
A collection of files (modules) that contain functions for use by other programs
questions.explain: Libraries let you reuse well-tested code instead of writing everything yourself.
questions.evidence: A library is a collection of files (called modules ) that contains functions for use by other programs.

questions.q: Which alias is commonly used for the Pandas library in code?
questions.explain: import pandas as pd is the community convention.
questions.evidence: The alias pd is commonly used to refer to the Pandas library in code.

questions.q: What is matplotlib?
options: A library for reading CSV files
The most widely used scientific plotting library in Python
A built-in function for printing tables
questions.explain: It draws time series, scatter plots and many other charts.
questions.evidence: matplotlib is the most widely used scientific plotting library in Python.

questions.q: What does a list do?
options: Stores many values in a single structure
questions.explain: Lists avoid having hundreds of separate variables like pressure_001, pressure_002…
questions.evidence: A list stores many values in a single structure.

questions.q: How must the first line and the body of a for loop be written?
options: The first line must end with a colon, and the body must be indented
The body must be in brackets
The first line must end with a semicolon
The loop must be written on a single line
questions.explain: Python uses the colon and indentation to know which statements belong to the loop.
questions.evidence: The first line of the for loop must end with a colon, and the body must be indented.

questions.q: In Unix, what does 'globbing' mean?
options: Matching a set of files with a pattern
Counting the lines in a file
questions.explain: Patterns like data/*.csv let a loop process many files.
questions.evidence: In Unix, the term "globbing" means "matching a set of files with a pattern".

questions.q: What is the scope of a variable?
options: The part of a program that can 'see' that variable
The number of times it changes
questions.explain: Variables created inside a function are local to it; global variables are visible everywhere.
questions.evidence: The scope of a variable is the part of a program that can 'see' that variable.

questions.q: Why does coding style matter, according to the lesson?
options: Python refuses to run badly formatted code
It is required to use pandas
Code is read much more often than it is written
questions.explain: Readable code (for example following PEP 8) is easier to share, review and fix.
questions.evidence: Code is read much more often than it is written

questions.q: What can the cells of a Jupyter notebook contain?
questions.explain: Mixing code and explanation is what makes notebooks useful.
questions.evidence: Each notebook contains one or more cells that contain code, text, or images.

questions.q: How does Command mode differ from Edit mode in a notebook?
options: Command mode edits notebook-level features; Edit mode changes a cell's content
Edit mode runs the whole notebook
questions.explain: Press Esc to leave Edit mode.
questions.evidence: Command mode allows you to edit notebook-level features, and Edit mode changes the content of cells.

questions.q: How do you turn the current cell into a Markdown cell?
options: Enter Command mode (Esc) and press M
questions.explain: Markdown cells hold formatted text.
questions.evidence: Turn the current cell into a Markdown cell by entering the Command mode

questions.q: A cell contains several calculations. What does Python show as the cell's output?
options: The result of the first calculation
The result of the last calculation
questions.explain: Use print to show other values.
questions.evidence: Python returns the output of the last calculation.

questions.q: Can a notebook's code be run from the command line?
options: Yes, once it is exported as a Python script
Only if it has no Markdown
questions.explain: Scripts use the .py extension.
questions.evidence: Notebooks can be exported as Python scripts that can be run from the command line.

questions.q: What do other Jupyter kernels let you do?
options: Run code in other languages, such as R or Julia, in JupyterLab
questions.explain: The kernel is what executes the code.
questions.evidence: Using other Jupyter kernels for other programming languages would let us write and execute code in other programming languages in the same JupyterLab interface

questions.q: What must happen before a variable can be used?
options: It must be created by assigning it a value
questions.explain: Using it first gives a NameError.
questions.evidence: Variables must be created before they are used.

questions.q: How does print separate the items you pass to it?
questions.explain: For example: Ahmed is 42 years old.
questions.evidence: print automatically puts a single space between items to separate them

questions.q: When you treat a string like a list, what are its elements?
questions.explain: So indexing a string gives one character.
questions.evidence: Whenever we treat a string as if it were a list, the string's elements are its individual characters.

questions.q: What does the lesson warn about copying and pasting someone else's code?
options: It's risky unless you understand exactly what it does
questions.explain: Asking a more experienced colleague is another good option.
questions.evidence: copying and pasting code written by somebody else is risky unless you understand exactly what it is doing

questions.q: Which are commonly used built-in functions?
questions.explain: Built-ins are available without importing anything.
questions.evidence: Commonly-used built-in functions include max , min , and round

questions.q: Why did max and min raise TypeErrors in the exercise?
options: Python doesn't have max or min
The correct number of parameters wasn't supplied
questions.explain: Functions expect particular kinds and numbers of arguments.
questions.evidence: max and min return TypeErrors in this case because the correct number of parameters was not supplied

questions.q: If you use AI tools to help write code, what do you still need?
options: The skills to judge whether the answers are right and fix errors
Nothing — the AI is always right
questions.explain: Understanding comes before trusting generated code.
questions.evidence: You need the knowledge and skills to be able to understand these responses, to judge whether or not they are accurate, and to fix any errors in the code it offers you.

questions.q: Are the words 'library' and 'module' interchangeable?
options: They are often used interchangeably, since many libraries are a single module
questions.explain: Strictly, a library is a collection of modules.
questions.evidence: the terms are often used interchangeably, especially since many libraries only consist of a single module

questions.q: What is Pandas widely used for?
questions.explain: It is usually imported with the alias pd.
questions.evidence: Pandas is a widely-used Python library for statistics, particularly on tabular data.

questions.q: Which library is Pandas built on top of?
questions.explain: So most NumPy array methods also work on Pandas objects.
questions.evidence: Pandas is built on top of the Numpy library

questions.q: What makes Pandas so attractive for data work?
options: Powerful access to records, handling of missing values and relational operations
questions.explain: It brings database-like operations to Python.
questions.evidence: What makes Pandas so attractive is the powerful interface to access individual records of the table, proper handling of missing values, and relational-databases operations between DataFrames.

questions.q: How does a numerical slice (iloc[0:2]) differ from a named slice (loc['a':'b'])?
options: They give exactly the same output
Named slices omit the first element
The numerical slice omits the final index; the named slice includes the final element
questions.explain: A common source of off-by-one surprises.
questions.evidence: a numerical slice, 0:2, omits the final index (i.e. index 2) in the range provided, while a named slice, 'gdpPercap_1952':'gdpPercap_1962', includes the final element

questions.q: When selecting from a DataFrame, what does : on its own mean?
questions.explain: For example, data.loc['Denmark', :] selects a whole row.
questions.evidence: Use : on its own to mean all columns or all rows.

questions.q: In matplotlib, what does the format string 'g--' produce?
questions.explain: 'b-' would be a blue solid line.
questions.evidence: b- is a blue line, g-- is a green dashed line

questions.q: Which plot shows the relationship between two data sets?
options: A time series plot of one variable
questions.explain: Time series plots show one variable over time.
questions.evidence: Create a scatter plot showing relationship between two data sets.

questions.q: What does it mean that Python lists are mutable?
options: They can be modified in place
questions.explain: Strings, by contrast, are immutable.
questions.evidence: In contrast, lists are mutable : they can be modified in place.

questions.q: How does extend differ from append?
questions.explain: append adds a single item to the end.
questions.evidence: extend is similar to append , but it allows you to combine two lists

questions.q: What changes on each iteration of a for loop?
questions.explain: It takes the next value from the collection each time.
questions.evidence: The loop variable, number , is what changes for each iteration of the loop.

questions.q: Which loop pattern aggregates values, such as a running total?
questions.explain: Start a variable at zero and add to it in each iteration.
questions.evidence: Write for loops that use the Accumulator pattern to aggregate values.

questions.q: What does an if statement do?
options: Repeats code a fixed number of times
Controls whether a block of code is executed
questions.explain: It is properly called a conditional statement.
questions.evidence: An if statement (more properly called a conditional statement) controls whether some block of code is executed or not.

questions.q: When should you use parentheses in a condition?
questions.explain: Just like in arithmetic, parentheses make intent clear.
questions.evidence: you can and should use parentheses whenever there is possible ambiguity

questions.q: Why break a program down into functions?
options: To make it run in parallel automatically
To make it easier to understand
questions.explain: Functions encapsulate complexity as a single 'thing'.
questions.evidence: Break programs down into functions to make them easier to understand.

questions.q: How are the arguments in a function call matched up?
questions.explain: Parameters receive the values passed in the call.
questions.evidence: Arguments in a function call are matched to its defined parameters.

questions.q: When are functions most useful?
options: When they can operate on different data
questions.explain: Parameters let one function serve many inputs.
questions.evidence: Functions are most useful when they can operate on different data.

questions.q: What does encapsulating complexity in a function let us do?
questions.explain: You can use the function without thinking about its insides.
questions.evidence: Encapsulate complexity so that we can treat it as a single

questions.q: Which keyword begins a function definition in Python?
questions.explain: It is followed by the name, parameters and an indented block.
questions.evidence: Begin the definition of a new function with def

questions.q: How does a function give a value back to its caller?
questions.explain: print only displays a value; return hands it back.
questions.evidence: Functions may return a result to their caller using return
